questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Cycling in one old bike country and one new one
How to learn to ride a bike safely as an adult
Why electric bikes are dangerous in big cities
The best and most famous bike races in Europe
questions.why: Neil says they'll visit two countries: one with a long cycling history and one where it's just starting.

questions.q: According to Becca, why are more people in Britain choosing to cycle?
options: Because cars are now banned in most city centres
Because bikes have become very cheap to buy
Because trains and buses are far too expensive
It's healthy and green, and e-bikes make it easier
questions.why: She says people cycle for health and the environment, and electric bikes make it more accessible.

questions.q: What does Meredith Glaser say changed for bikes in the Netherlands during the industrial era?
options: They were banned from city streets for many years
They went from a toy for the rich to daily transport
They became mainly used for racing and sport
They were quickly replaced by cheaper cars
questions.why: She says the bike went from a toy for rich people to an everyday tool for transportation.

questions.q: What helped make bikes cheaper in the Netherlands in the 1890s?
options: Government payments
Imports from other countries
New factories
Lower taxes
questions.why: Becca says new factories made bikes cheaper to buy.

questions.q: According to Martin Tillman, why do Gulf cities want to encourage cycling?
options: To reduce the number of tourists
To save money on roads
Because people there have stopped buying cars
To rank highly for quality of life and liveability
questions.why: He says the cities are competitive and want high global rankings, and cycling is part of quality of life.

questions.q: How much cycle track has already been built in Dubai?
options: 600 kilometres
95,000 miles
60 kilometres
6,000 kilometres
questions.why: Neil says Dubai's planners hope the 600km of cycle tracks already built will make it more attractive.

questions.q: What does Martin mean when he says Dubai's cycling is not 'a copy and paste' of Holland?
options: Dubai wants to be better than Holland at cycling
Dubai has no interest in other countries
Dubai is learning the main ideas, not copying exactly
Dubai will buy its bikes from Holland
questions.why: He says it isn't a copy and paste; 'we're looking for the principles'.

questions.q: What has Dubai done to help people cycle in the heat?
options: Only opened cycle tracks at night
Created water stations and shaded rest areas
Built covered cycle tunnels everywhere
Given free electric bikes to tourists
questions.why: Neil says water stations and shaded rest areas have been created for cycling in the heat.
